articles.title: Travis Kelce incident could trigger costly NFL punishment for Chargers defender after controversial on-field hit
articles.summary: The NFL could impose a five-figure fine on Los Angeles Chargers linebacker Daiyan Henley if the league determines that his tackle on Kansas City Chiefs
articles.body: The NFL could impose a five-figure fine on Los Angeles Chargers linebacker Daiyan Henley if the league determines that his tackle on Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce violated its ban on hip-drop tackles. The incident occurred during the Chiefs’ 22-6 win on October 18, when Kelce appeared to hurt his ankle and briefly left the game. He returned to finish the contest, but the tackle has drawn scrutiny because of the technique involved. No official ruling or fine had been announced in the report published by Heavy, leaving Henley’s potential punishment unresolved.Daiyan Henley faces scrutiny over tackle on Travis KelceHenley’s tackle came during Kansas City’s opening offensive drive. Video of the play circulated online, prompting criticism from Chiefs fans and analysts who believed the linebacker had used an illegal hip-drop technique. Kelce’s apparent ankle injury added to the concern, although he was able to return to the field.The NFL bans hip-drop tackles when a defender unweights himself, swivels his hips and drops onto a ball carrier’s legs. The technique can place significant stress on the lower body, which is why the league has targeted it through its player-safety rules. The key question is whether Henley’s movement met all the criteria for a violation, not simply whether Kelce was hurt.Officials may miss the details of a tackle during live action, but the league can review the footage after a game. That process gives the NFL a chance to assess plays that were not penalized on the field. Heavy reported that the league had not officially confirmed a review of Henley’s tackle, so any suggestion that a fine is imminent remains speculative.Kelce’s return offered some relief for Kansas City, but it does not settle the question of whether the tackle broke league rules. The NFL can assess a play based on its mechanics even when the player involved avoids a serious injury.Henley could face a fine of nearly $18,000The financial risk is significant even if the NFL ultimately treats the incident as a first-time violation. According to the league’s official website, a first offense involving an illegal hip-drop tackle carries a baseline fine of $17,911. A repeat violation can raise the amount to $23,882, putting Henley at risk of a costly penalty if the league rules against him.The league’s response could also draw attention because of the history of injuries associated with this type of tackle. In 2023, a similar tackling motion ended Baltimore Ravens tight end Mark Andrews’ season. Kelce avoided that outcome, returning after briefly heading to the sideline, but the play has renewed questions about how consistently defenders follow the NFL’s restrictions.Chiefs coach Andy Reid offered a reassuring update after the game, saying Kelce might be sore but would still “be ok.” That was encouraging news for Kansas City, which had already secured the win. The focus now shifts to whether the NFL considers Henley’s technique a punishable offense.For the Chargers, the incident adds another concern after a sixth consecutive loss. A fine would not change the result against Kansas City, but it would put an individual disciplinary issue alongside the team’s wider struggles. Until the league issues its findings, however, Henley remains at risk of a penalty rather than a player who has been officially fined.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘Humiliating’ – NFL’s Cincinnati Bengals’ treatment of Vice President JD Vance draws fan attention
articles.summary: U. S. Vice President JD Vance went inside the Cincinnati Bengals locker room after their practice on October 21 to greet the players, but it didn’t go to pla...
articles.body:
U.S. Vice President JD Vance went inside the Cincinnati Bengals locker room after their practice on October 21 to greet the players, but it didn't go to plan.

President Donald Trump has found ways to ingratiate himself with many people in the sports world, bringing out multiple NFL players and legends to publicly support and endorse him for the job he is doing as the country's President.

Vice President Vance tried to interact with an NFL team after their latest practice session and found the reception much colder than what the President has received around athletes over the last two years.

JD Vance's cold interaction with the Bengals has fans talking

Vice President Vance stood in the locker room as the Bengals players finished practice, with nobody except TE Drew Sample shaking Vance's hand, with the other players seemingly ignoring Vance's presence.

Another video did show Vance interacting with star WR Ja'Marr Chase, but outside of that, it seemed to be a very cold reception, something that fans did not ignore on social media.

"One guy on the entire team acknowledges the existence of the vice president of the United States who is standing just feet away. Humiliating," said one fan, labelling this as a humiliating experience for the VP .

"I've never seen a group of people less enthusiastic to meet the vice president. They barely looked his way," said another fan .

"Looks like he got ignored by 95% of the roster lol," was the main takeaway for one fan .

"interesting that most of them ignored him," observed a fan .

"Good for the Bengal players. Vance is an obnoxious jerk," were the thoughts of another fan .

The Bengals were likely exhausted after an intensive training session before a high-stakes clash against the 4-2 Baltimore Ravens.

Vance is an Ohio native and likely roots for the Bengals, so he will probably feel negatively about this interaction. At least he did get visible support from TE Sample and spoke to Chase in the hallway; otherwise, this would have looked a lot worse for the popular support the VP carries.

articles.title: From $275 million to $325 million: How Patrick and Brittany Mahomes’ soccer club grew in one year
articles.summary: The Kansas City Current are now worth $325 million, according to Forbes' 2026 NWSL valuations.
articles.body: The Kansas City Current are now worth $325 million, according to Forbes' 2026 NWSL valuations. That puts the club co-owned by Patrick and Brittany Mahomes second in the league, behind only Angel City FC at $340 million. A year ago Forbes had the Current at $275 million, so the value rose about 18 percent in twelve months.Kansas City Current valuation rises from $275 million to $325 millionThe numbers are simple. Forbes valued the Current at $275 million in 2025 and raised that to $325 million this spring. Angel City still leads, and its edge grew from $5 million last year to $15 million. Kansas City is still close enough that the top spot is not out of reach, though the gap moved the wrong way.Growth was not unique to Kansas City, and it was not even the fastest. Forbes says the average NWSL team, leaving out Denver and Boston in their debut seasons, is worth about $200 million, up 49 percent from last year. Angel City rose 21 percent. Bay FC, San Diego and Washington all grew faster than the Current's 18 percent, and the Spirit jumped 65 percent. Kansas City just started from a higher base, so each point of growth is worth more dollars.Stability explains part of it. The NWSL runs on a salary cap and has no relegation, so owners can plan years ahead instead of fearing a bad season will wreck the balance sheet. Investors pay for that kind of predictability, and each new expansion fee pushes the numbers higher.Revenue backs up the price. The list shows the Current at roughly $38 million, level with Angel City. Forbes says the club could climb out of operating losses as soon as this year. Red ink is not rare in pro sports. Twelve of 30 MLB teams and 16 of 29 MLS teams posted negative operating income in 2025.How the Mahomes family became KC Current ownersBrittany Mahomes played professional soccer in Iceland, and that background explains why the couple's name is on this club. She joined Angie and Chris Long in the ownership group, and Patrick came aboard in 2022, making him one of the first active NFL players with a stake in an NWSL team. Soccer is not his only side bet. He also owns pieces of the Kansas City Royals, Sporting Kansas City and Alpine F1.The club has kept its public message simple. Its statement reads: "When Angie Long, Chris Long, and Brittany Mahomes brought this NWSL franchise to Kansas City, they were clear in their commitment to do it right, for the players and for the city."Results on the field were less tidy when the list came out in April. Kansas City sat 14th under Armas, the first former MLS head coach to move into the NWSL, even after winning the 2025 Shield.Buyers are not waiting for a turnaround. Columbus will pay a $205 million expansion fee to join in 2028, while Denver paid $110 million in 2025. Against those numbers, $325 million for a club with a Shield and a purpose-built stadium looks less like a stretch.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: The NFC East offers a turnaround chance for one struggling team - Daily Slop
articles.summary: Which team will it be? The Commanders next 8 opponents have combined record of 17-29-1; 6 have 4 or 5 losses in 6 games
articles.body:
Editor's note: Each day, Hogs Haven compiles a collection of articles, podcasts & tweets from around the web to keep you in touch with the Commanders, the NFC East, the NFL and sports in general, with a sprinkling of other stuff. Enjoy!

Even with the second-worst record in the conference, the Commanders are only two games out of first place in their division. And if the team makes the necessary adjustments over their week off , that deficit could shrink quickly.

When the Commanders return to the field, they'll play the Philadelphia Eagles at home without quarterback Jalen Hurts, who is done for the year with a scary blood clot situation.

After that, they'll play the biggest disappointment in the NFL — with the only possible exception of the team they share a stadium with — the Los Angeles Rams.

If the Commanders win both of those games, they're right back in business.

They'll face the New York Giants on the road, who they should've beaten at home . They'll host the ever-inconsistent Cincinnati Bengals. They'll visit the Arizona Cardinals and Tennessee Titans, two teams they should beat regardless of the location. Then they'll host the Houston Texans and Atlanta Falcons, both currently sub-.500 operations.

The Commanders should win at least five of those games. They can probably win all of them if they bring their best.

[U]n 2020, Washington started the season 2-7 and rallied to make the playoffs at 7-9.

This Commanders team is substantially more talented than that one was. That squad's regular-season quarterbacks were Dwayne Haskins, Kyle Allen, and a one-legged Alex Smith. Its second-leading receiver was Cam Sims.

This team has Jayden Daniels under center. Even without McLaurin, Stefon Diggs, third-round rookie Antonio Williams, and Treylon Burks are still here. And first-year linebacker Sonny Styles is putting together a Defensive Rookie of the Year-caliber campaign just as Chase Young did then .

All the Commanders need to do is stay relatively healthy the rest of the way and let the rest of the NFC East keep imploding. Once they pick up one or two wins, which they'd better be able to do with this stretch coming up, they'll have momentum and vibes on their side.

It looks bleak now. But that can change, and the bye week is the perfect time to refresh and map out the road ahead.

To read more of this article, CLICK HERE

[T]he reason they need to give him more looks is clear: he creates separation like no one else on the roster, and even though his snap share has stayed steady (hovering in the high 60s of late, even in London when McLaurin was out nursing a hamstring), he's criminally underused in David Blough's system.

Against San Francisco, Williams ran 35 routes but had only four targets, catching three for 50 yards. All four targets came on third down in the fourth quarter, and his three catches accounted for Washington's only successful third-down conversions of the night. In an offense looking for answers, why ignore one?

A glance over Williams' numbers above makes a major case for him to be involved earlier and more often, including plays where he's the intended first read. PFF credits him with 69 run-blocking snaps and a 51.5 run-blocking grade, leaving room for improvement if Washington expands his role in two-receiver formations.

The bye gives Blough time to make Williams a bigger part of the plan from the opening drive. Give him designed opportunities on first and second down. Washington has a lot of production to replace with McLaurin out, and Williams has already shown he can handle more of that work.

Steve Wilks has joined Washington's defensive staff to help Dan Quinn and Daronte Jones, but his role comes with an important limitation

According to NFL Insiders Mike Garafolo and Ian Rapoport, the Washington Commanders hired Steve Wilks to help the defensive staff ahead of the game against the 49ers. The decision to hire Wilks was made back in September, but he didn't start working with the team until last week. Wilks will assist with game planning and will work under Quinn and defensive coordinator Daronte Jones; he will not be with the team on game days.

It's important to stress that Wilks has no playcalling duties and is there to make the staff's job easier. The real gauge will come after the bye, when everyone will see whether any consistency changes are visible, as adding another football mind doesn't guarantee anything changes on the field.

Dan Quinn bought himself time with the fight Washington showed in San Francisco, and the Commanders have already added Steve Wilks to help the defensive staff

The defense is where Wilks comes in. Jones' unit has struggled to adjust after halftime, as we noted earlier this month , and Odafe Oweh's slow start on a $100 million deal hasn't helped. Sonny Styles, the NFL's top defensive rookie at the quarter mark, gives Wilks a young piece to build around. Daron Payne, who has 12 sacks over the four seasons since his 2022 breakout, landed third on FOX Sports' list of the best players who could be available before Nov. 10.

The offense took its own hit. Terry McLaurin tore his patellar tendon and will miss the rest of the season, Quinn said, per The Athletic's Jonathan Jones , which leaves Daniels without his top target and the front office with trade options to explore .

Download the SB Nation app Commanders fans, take command of game day!

Follow the action and share every cheer, question and instant reaction with fellow fans on the SB Nation app.

Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android .

The Commanders get two weeks to fix third downs, the run game and Odafe Oweh's pass rush before a 2-4 Eagles team brings Tanner McKee to Landover on Nov 1

Two weeks is a long time to sit on a 23-17 loss, and the Washington Commanders will spend their bye trying to fix the reason they keep losing close games. Monday night in Santa Clara, they converted 3 of 12 third downs against the 49ers. For the season they are 25 of 81, a 30.9% rate that ranks 31st in the NFL ahead of only Cleveland, according to NFL.com .

Washington went 0 of 4 on third down in the first half Monday, and the offense was flagged seven times for 66 yards. Holding calls on Josh Conerly Jr., Lucas Patrick and Brandon Coleman pushed drives backward, and Chris Paul's face mask erased a go-ahead 31-yard touchdown run by Jeremy McNichols. We wrote that the offensive line keeps undoing what Jayden Daniels builds, and the third-down numbers back that up.

Baun is the reason the Eagles can survive without much else. He had 12 tackles, a tackle for loss and two pass breakups in the 24-22 opener at Lincoln Financial Field. Washington targeted him six times in coverage and gained minus-2 yards, and PFF gave him a 90.6 defensive grade, per the Eagles . He and Jalen Carter stuffed a third-and-1 in the first quarter, and Baun dropped a screen for a 7-yard loss in the second. Daniels needs manageable distances, and his line has to stop handing back 10 yards at a time.

On Wednesday, PFF ranked the Commanders offensive line 20th in the league through six weeks.

"Washington's front five combined to allow 18 pressures, eight of which were either sacks or quarterback hits," wrote PFF's Gordon McGuinness . "Right tackle Josh Conerly Jr. permitted six pressures on 51 pass-blocking snaps, a mark that led the team."

Commanders writer Chad Ryan posted a chart on X that showed Daniels has had, on average, just 1.5 seconds before the pocket has collapsed on him this season. That's the shortest amount of time in the league.

Entering Week 6, the Commanders were third in offensive line combinations according to Next Gen Stats.

But Quinn was very clear Tuesday. He won't stop shuffling the offensive line until the unit plays a lot better.

Laremy Tunsil has not been on the field since he tore his triceps in training camp, but that does not mean he is absent from the Washington Commanders' facility.

Actually, the five-time Pro Bowler is around quite a bit, and it has been a benefit for the team's young offensive linemen.

"I think it's been a blessing," Josh Conerly said. "And it means a lot to us, as a group and for me personally."

Tunsil might not be able to help the Commanders protect Jayden Daniels on game days, but the veteran is still finding ways to contribute while receiving treatment for his injury. He has been offering advice to the rest of the offensive linemen in the room and providing guidance on how they can improve their skill set. To the Commanders, it is more evidence of Tunsil's leadership and how it has elevated the roster.

"I'm sick about the ending," Quinn said.

He should be. A win under these circumstances — against an unbeaten, smack-you-into-next-week team against which he trailed 23-3 in the fourth quarter — would have righted not only Quinn's own ship, but would have yanked the Commanders back into the division race, leapfrogging the 2-4 Cowboys and Eagles.

"We went out and we competed hard, but competed only gets you so far in this league," Daniels said. "We got to do whatever it takes to win the game, and we didn't win."

Pick that quote up and attribute it to any Commander from so many games over the past year-and-change. It gets them nowhere. Since the beginning of last season, according to TruMedia, only five teams have a worse point differential than Washington — Tennessee, the New York Jets, Las Vegas, Arizona and Miami.

If that seems like the dregs of the league, well, that's the company the Commanders now keep. At some point, your new house just settles into becoming part of the neighborhood.

The bye week, though, can't just be about the players. If Quinn is to survive — and that's not just for a Nov. 1 home game against Philadelphia, but into 2027 — he's going to have to do some serious self-examination. Right now, he is good — and honest — about identifying problems. He's not so good at fixing them.

The fact that a 20-point deficit didn't spiral into another embarrassment likely gives Quinn the tiniest bit of wiggle room. A schedule that opens up — the 2-4 Eagles without Jalen Hurts, the 2-4 Rams who are a mess, Arizona and Tennessee beyond — provides opportunity.

Check out the top photos of the Washington Commanders during their Week 6 matchup with the San Francisco 49ers

Eagles coach Nick Sirianni has been fined $250,000 for his conduct toward game officials, according to Sports Illustrated's Albert Breer , though the financial penalty reportedly includes an option to avoid payment. Breer reported that Sirianni, Patriots coach Mike Vrabel and Jets coach Aaron Glenn each received $250,000 fines. The penalties are in abeyance, meaning they are on hold and could be rescinded for good behavior.

The discipline surfaced as league officials addressed tensions involving coaches, players, and officials during this week's owners meetings. Available reporting did not identify the specific incident or pattern of behavior that prompted Sirianni's fine. For Sirianni, the development adds another issue during a difficult stretch for Philadelphia. The Eagles have lost four straight after a 2-0 start and enter Monday night's matchup against Dallas looking for an offensive turnaround.

[I]ts conditional status matters. The penalty serves as a warning with potential financial consequences as the NFL tries to improve interactions with its officials.

First off, the Cowboys are still very much in the playoff race due to the poor state of the NFC East division. For the second week in a row, all four teams in the NFC East failed to win, leaving the division up for grabs.

As much as many of us would like to see Schottenheimer replaced after his many coaching gaffs, that seems highly unlikely given the state of the NFC East division and the possibility of the Cowboys coming out on top. After all, who would step in to replace him?

It's up to them to start executing and playing better. For the sake for mental health, all of us are probably hoping they can do so.

At 2-4, the Cowboys still have time to turn things around. The NFC East is not out of reach, and there are enough talented players on this roster to make a run if the team can finally put together a complete performance. Writing off the season in October would be premature.

But it is fair to ask what this team is building toward if the same problems keep showing up every week. If Dallas cannot establish a clear identity, clean up its mistakes or get consistent performances from its coaching staff and leaders, then talk about the draft will become more prominent.

Dallas does not need to panic after six games, but it does need to be honest about what it is seeing. The Cowboys have talent, and they've shown flashes of progress on both sides of the ball. What they have not shown is the ability to put it all together for four quarters, consistently.

Right now, the Cowboys do not look like a team that is one adjustment away from contention. They look like a team searching for answers — and running out of time to find them.

[T]he Cowboys [can't be excused] from not properly accounting for if Schotty could keep the offense consistently performing while they went "all in" on a defensive makeover, and now the organization is paying the cost of having more holes in the boat than patches – seeing the defense, offense, and special teams all have a hand in ugly losses.

More simply put, the Cowboys "run it back" approach to hyping up all 11 starters returning on offense as a huge positive is not working, and this is another thing we've seen before as fans. Whenever proper attention isn't given to any one position group or facet of the game at large in the offseason, they regress to the point of being a problem.

The low hanging fruit of a take on the job he did in these areas in 2025 was that everything offensively was under too much fire because of the horrid defense, so all things considered because of that he did alright.

Last time out, the Cowboys defense held the Packers to six points in the second half, and the Cowboys still abandoned the run game and didn't make much noise in a comeback attempt.

The Cowboys offense banked on experience to be dominant in 2026, but they're paying an ultimate cost right now for an underperforming head coach and play-caller dragging the entire ceiling this team has down in a division that's never, ever been more winnable.

It feels like the move to McCarthy was inevitable since the Giants surrendered a fifth-round draft pick to acquire him. In an ideal world, Harbaugh might have waited until after the BYE week to make this move. Then again, the Giants have not been living in an ideal world since the moment Jaxson Dart was lost for the season.

Fact is, the Giants have been in survival mode. They are going to be in survival mode all season, doing the best they can with backup quarterbacks they did not plan on playing.

McCarthy is not Dart. He does, though, give the Giants the opportunity to be the offense they want to be rather than the offense they have to be with Winston. There is more upside there, though nobody knows if McCarthy will be better or worse than Winston has been.

The Giants went 2-1-1 in four games with Winston starting after Jaxson Dart was lost for the season with a knee injury, McCarthy, though, closer approximates Dart's skill set than the immobile, 32-year-old Winston. The Giants spent the offseason building an offense that would incorporate Dart's running ability. That was lost with Winston. McCarthy, 23, is not the runner Dart is, but does give offensive coordinator Matt Nagy the ability to access that portion of the playbook.

Harbaugh is not worried about how much of the offense McCarthy can run.

"He's got the gameplan down," Harbaugh said. "I think he had it down last week pretty fully, even more so this week. It has been tailored a little more toward his direction, probably. He'll be ready to go."

Harbaugh would not commit to McCarthy being the starter for the remainder of the season.

"Life is day-to-day, minute-to-minute. There's really no guarantees," Harbaugh said. "I would never say that anything is permanent in football or life. That's the plan going forward."

The "NFC Least" bit was funny last week. Now it's just sort of sad. For the second straight week, the entire division failed to muster a win, despite every team playing. It's the first time in NFL history that's happened, and it speaks to what kind of year it's been for a division that's been ravaged by injuries and decorated in disappointment. At the moment, the 3-2-1 Giants are pacing this lackluster race, but they can't even decide on a starting quarterback (or a running back). The Cowboys and Eagles follow at 2-4, with Philly trying to figure out what to do next at QB after placing Jalen Hurts on injured reserve, while Dallas is simply trying to find any momentum on either side of the ball. Finally, there's the 1-4-1 Commanders, who have actually looked plucky since Jayden Daniels' return, yet continue to make all the wrong kinds of headlines.

What person in this division is facing the most heat?

There is a strong case to say Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni is facing the most heat — both deserved and undeserved. He spent Monday afternoon repeating that he was not a medical expert when reporters asked him how the Eagles managed Hurts' blood clots . Indeed, he is not the authority on the medical situation. But it was an organizational misstep not to make those with authority on the situation available (the team's medical staff reports to general manager Howie Roseman), or to at the very least brief Sirianni with necessary information. Meanwhile, the on-field product on offense is miserable.

The Commanders coach was eight days out from a nearly unforgivable game-management situation against the Giants when he introduced the possibility that he didn't know what down it was. Quinn's answer for that fourth-down play Monday night in San Francisco — that he absolutely knew what down it was, and that someone asked him if the Commanders could kick a field goal — is being scrutinized in the aftermath. It's not an indication he's making something up. It's an indication that his every action — every timeout, every fourth-down, every personnel deployment — is under the microscope . That's what happens when you win only four times in your last 18 tries.

Will the team you cover be a buyer before the deadline? Should they be?

There's just no way. The Commanders shouldn't be. They won't be. And that's even if they win their next two games against the 2-4 Eagles and the 2-4 Rams. (Is everyone out there 2-4?) It's not just that their big "buy" move in the 2024 season, cornerback Marshon Lattimore, flopped. It's that they have seven picks in the 2027 draft, and they clearly need as many of those to hit to rebuild a roster that, three years into the reign of general manager Adam Peters, needs both high-end talent and quality depth. If the Commanders make this a win-now year, it'll be because they methodically stack wins against a slightly easier schedule filled with opponents who are dealing with serious injuries and other issues. It won't be because they make a splashy move for a veteran player, sacrificing precious draft capital in the process.

The hidden world of technology, chaos, and split-second conversations behind every play

[ Bill-in-Bangkok : I read this entire (and very long) article. If you have any interest in the topic, you might well find this deep dive fascinating. I only provided the intro paragraphs in this excerpt because it was too hard to mine a single nugget out of this article ]

The hidden world inside NFL headsets is as complex and strategic as it is chaotic: a textured audio landscape of intense competition, stress, dramatically shifting emotions, unwritten rules and even absurdity.

From moment to moment, anything can happen.

Batteries die, communications get fuzzy (especially at certain stadiums) and paranoia flows. One coach demands silence as he calls a play, racing the play clock while his quarterback waits anxiously. Another flips channels to share praise or strategy, or to curse at someone.

A desperate assistant sneaks to a urinal midgame, standing shoulder-to-shoulder with fans, headset still over his ears — his relief disrupted by the voice of his furious boss looking for him on the sideline. Headsets erupt with joy after a touchdown or sack. A play call fails, and it's swearing or worse: awkward silence.

"In the moment, it can be like, 'Holy s—, what the f— are we doing? How is this a billion-dollar industry?'" Detroit Lions offensive coordinator Drew Petzing said. "And then there are other moments where you're like, 'Wow, that was so impressive.'"

We talked to more than two dozen current and former coaches, players, analysts, equipment managers and other experts about the relationships, technology and split-second decision-making that they see and hear every week but fans never do.

We take you inside the headset, from how the system works to what actually happens during every game.

articles.title: Week 7 TNF Fantasy Football Wide Receiver Start 'Em, Sit 'Em: A.J. Brown vs. Luther Burden
articles.summary: Deciding between A.J. Brown and Luther Burden III for Week 7 TNF? Get our stats-driven analysis, defensive rankings, and final start/sit verdict.
articles.body:
Heading into Week 7 of the 2026 NFL season, fantasy football managers are still dealing with an ever-evolving running back landscape, as well as ongoing bye weeks. With the New England Patriots and Chicago Bears facing each other on Thursday Night Football, this week presents us with an interesting Start/Sit decision between two stud wide receivers: New England's A.J. Brown and Chicago's Luther Burden III.

Let's break down both players' recent play, matchup dynamics, and injury news in this Week 7 Thursday Night Football Wide Receiver Start 'Em, Sit 'Em debate.

A.J. Brown enters Week 7 looking to shake off some rust after returning to action last week. In his Week 6 return against the New York Jets, he hauled in 3 catches on 10 targets for 27 yards, battling a few drops as he gets up to speed with Drake Maye in the Patriots' offense. Despite the slow statistical line in his first game back, Brown's elite downfield tracking, physical route-running, and alpha target share give him a massive ceiling every time he steps on the field.

As Brown looks for his first touchdown of the year, he faces a stiff Chicago Bears secondary that surrenders 211.8 passing yards per game (ranking 14th in the NFL). While Chicago's defense does a strong job keeping games condensed and limiting chunk plays, Brown's volume and red-zone profile mean he can break a slate open if he and Maye hit their stride on a short week (especially with Romeo Doubs on injured reserve and some extra targets open for the taking).

Luther Burden III enters Week 7 riding a massive wave of sophomore momentum, averaging 11.2 PPR fantasy points per game (totaling 55.8 PPR points across five games). He is fresh off a brilliant performance in Week 6 against the Atlanta Falcons, where he secured all 8 of his targets for 95 yards, acting as Caleb Williams' favorite security blanket. Burden has quickly built a heavy footprint in the slot and intermediate game, posting a 31-361-1 receiving line on 43 targets through his first six games.

Burden faces a tough test against a New England Patriots defense that surrenders roughly 209 passing yards per game and locks down opponents to just 18.8 points per game (5th-fewest in the NFL). While New England's physical secondary will try to bracket short-area routes (and he may draw Christian Gonzalez), Burden's expanding role, high target volume, and ability to generate yards after the catch in space make him a reliable weekly asset.

While Luther Burden III is riding high off a big 8-catch, 95-yard outing and offers a safer weekly target floor, A.J. Brown's unmatched physical ceiling and elite target command in New England keep him ahead in our Week 7 Wide Receiver Rankings . Don't get scared away by the drops in his first game back from injury last week. Brown will have the rust shaken off for Thursday Night Football.

articles.title: JJ McCarthy makes NFL history in comeback effort against the Giants
articles.summary: Ringo Chiu/Shutterstock.com McCarthy’s 243-yard performance puts Giants’ quarterback plans in focus J.J. McCarthy delivered a remarkable fourth-quarter perfo...
articles.body:
McCarthy's 243-yard performance puts Giants' quarterback plans in focus

J.J. McCarthy delivered a remarkable fourth-quarter performance against the New Orleans Saints on October 18, 2026, throwing for 243 yards after replacing Jameis Winston at quarterback. The New York Giants faced a 24-point deficit but mounted a late rally that brought them within one score of tying the game.

Despite McCarthy's passing production and 17 unanswered points, New York fell 34–27. On October 21, head coach John Harbaugh named McCarthy the Giants' starting quarterback for their Week 7 game against the Houston Texans.

New York started Jameis Winston at quarterback against New Orleans at MetLife Stadium. Winston threw two interceptions, including one early in the fourth quarter, before coach John Harbaugh replaced him with McCarthy.

The Giants trailed 34–10 when the quarterback change occurred. McCarthy entered with limited time remaining and immediately faced the challenge of moving the offense against a sizable deficit.

The Saints built a 34–10 lead after taking control of the game following New York's early advantage. Chris Olave caught an 18-yard touchdown pass from Tyler Shough early in the fourth quarter to extend New Orleans' lead.

With the Giants trailing by 24 points, J.J. McCarthy replaced Jameis Winston at quarterback. New York needed multiple scoring drives and defensive stops to have a chance of changing the result.

McCarthy's first appearance for the Giants did not begin smoothly, as he threw an interception on his first possession. The turnover added an early setback while New York attempted to close the gap against New Orleans.

However, McCarthy continued directing the offense after the mistake. He threw for 243 yards and a touchdown in just over 11 minutes, helping the Giants mount a late comeback before their 34–27 defeat.

New York began its late scoring surge when Tyrone Tracy Jr. scored a rushing touchdown with about seven minutes remaining. McCarthy helped the Giants move the ball as they attempted to cut into the Saints' lead.

The two-point conversion succeeded on a pass from McCarthy to tight end Isaiah Likely. The play reduced New Orleans' advantage to 34–18 and kept the Giants within reach of a closer finish.

McCarthy followed the Giants' first touchdown with another scoring drive against the Saints. He connected with Isaiah Likely for a touchdown pass during the fourth quarter as New York continued its comeback attempt.

The Giants attempted a two-point conversion after the score but did not convert. The touchdown brought New York closer to the Saints, although the Giants still needed additional points to complete the comeback.

McCarthy accumulated 243 passing yards during his fourth-quarter appearance against New Orleans. He produced that total in 11 minutes and 25 seconds after replacing Jameis Winston.

Despite throwing an interception on his first possession, McCarthy then led three scoring drives. His 243 passing yards tied the Giants' highest single-quarter total since at least 1991, and New York cut a 24-point deficit to 7 before losing 34–27.

McCarthy matches a Giants franchise mark

McCarthy's 243 passing yards were the second-most by a Giants quarterback in a fourth quarter. Eli Manning threw for 254 yards in the fourth quarter of a 36–25 loss to the Seattle Seahawks on October 9, 2011. McCarthy also matched Manning's 243-yard fourth quarter against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in 2012.

McCarthy produced his total in 11 minutes and 25 seconds after entering with New York trailing 34–10. Although the Giants lost 34–27, his late passing helped bring them within one score of the Saints.

Interesting fact : McCarthy was the 10th overall pick in the 2024 NFL Draft.

Wide receiver Malik Nabers played an important role in the Giants' passing attack against New Orleans. He recorded 12 receptions for 165 yards, making him one of the game's leading receiving contributors.

Nabers' production helped New York move the ball against the Saints. His performance also formed part of the wider evaluation of the Giants' offense following the 34–27 defeat and McCarthy's late appearance at quarterback.

Likely provides another receiving option

Tight end Isaiah Likely contributed to New York's offensive production against the Saints. He recorded six receptions for 99 yards and a touchdown, including a fourth-quarter scoring catch from McCarthy.

Likely's involvement gave the Giants another productive option in the passing game. His touchdown helped New York continue its rally, although the offense ultimately failed to complete the comeback.

New York scored 17 unanswered points in the final 11 minutes of its game against the Saints. The late surge included Tyrone Tracy Jr.'s rushing touchdown, McCarthy's touchdown pass to Isaiah Likely and a field goal by Dominic Zvada.

The Giants' defense also forced a turnover and three punts during the comeback attempt. Despite those contributions, New York remained seven points behind in the closing seconds and ultimately lost 34–27.

The Giants had one final opportunity to tie the game in the closing seconds. Facing fourth-and-one at the Saints' 14-yard line with 12 seconds remaining, McCarthy threw a pass intended for Likely in the back of the end zone.

The pass fell incomplete, ending New York's comeback attempt. The Saints held on for a 34–27 victory after allowing the Giants to score 17 unanswered points during the final 11 minutes.

A confrontation involving a stadium worker has brought attention to the interactions surrounding the Dallas Cowboys quarterback. Find out why Michael Irvin pointed to Dak Prescott's role in the stadium worker confrontation .

McCarthy's performance raises quarterback questions

McCarthy's fourth-quarter production led the Giants to reconsider their quarterback plan for Week 7. On October 19, head coach John Harbaugh said the team was still choosing between McCarthy and Winston for its October 25 game against the Houston Texans.

On October 21, Harbaugh announced that McCarthy would start in Houston, with Winston serving as the backup. Winston finished the Saints game with 152 passing yards, one touchdown and two interceptions, while McCarthy completed 11 of 21 passes for 243 yards, one touchdown and one interception.

A costly play by the New York Giants running back became a talking point after the matchup with Washington. Discover why Mike Tomlin criticized Cam Skattebo's mistake against the Commanders .

What do you think about McCarthy's performance, and should he start the Giants' next game? Like this post and share your thoughts in the comments!

articles.title: What channel is Patriots vs. Bears on tonight? Time, TV schedule
articles.summary: The Patriots and Bears will meet at 8:15 p.m. Thursday, Oct. 22, at Soldier Field in Chicago on Prime Video.
articles.body:
The Patriots (4-2) and Bears ( 4-2 ) will meet on Thursday, Oct. 22, at Soldier Field in Chicago. Here's what to know about the game:

What time will the Patriots face the Bears?

The Patriots and Bears will kick off at 8:15 p.m. Thursday, Oct. 22. The forecast for Chicago is clear skies with temperatures in the mid 50s.

See the Patriots vs. the Jets on Sunday, Oct. 18 at Gillette Stadium

Thursday's game will be broadcast by Amazon Prime Video . Al Michaels will handle play-by-play duties with Kirk Herbstreit as color analyst. Kaylee Hartung will report from the sidelines.

What to know about the Patriots before the game

The Patriots hold an 11-4 advantage in the overall regular-season meetings with the Bears. The Pats' .733 winning percentage is the highest against any NFC opponent. ... The only time the two teams have met in the postseason was in 1985 when the Bears defeated the Patriots, 46-10, in Super Bowl XX. ... New England's offensive line has multiple starters missing, and with the short week, quarterback Drake Maye could be under a lot of pressure against a defense that had five sacks against the Atlanta Falcons last week. ... Only the 0-6 Los Angeles Chargers have more turnovers (15) than the Pats (13) this season. ... Patriots receiver AJ Brown experienced a home debut last week that he'd rather forget. The star receiver had a career-high three dropped passes and also mishandled an onside kick that could have cost the Pats the game. Brown needs to revert to his old self, especially since receiver Romeo Doubs has been placed on injured reserve.

What to know about the Bears before the game

Chicago quarterback Caleb Williams returned to the field last week after a three-game absence because of an injured hamstring. He picked up where he left off as he passed for more than 300 yards and three touchdowns. His 72.5% completion rate leads the NFL's qualified QBs. ... The Bears rank No. 1 in rushing offense, averaging 160.7 yards, and average time of possession at 36 minutes. ... Bears defensive end Montez Sweat , who led the Bears in sacks last year, will be serving the second game of a two-game suspension on Thursday for violating the NFL's performance-enhancing substances policy. ... Chicago running back Kyle Monangai , one of the game's leading rushers who went down with a turf toe injury a couple of weeks ago, is still listed as week-to-week but is not expected to be ready for Thursday night's game.

articles.title: Adam Schefter pushes back on rumors of Peyton Manning taking Colts' GM job
articles.summary: It certainly seems that the rumors of Peyton Manning being a candidate for the Colts' general manager position were overblown.
articles.body:
Earlier this week, Dan Patrick caused a stir when he reported on his radio program that the Indianapolis Colts ' "first call" after firing general manager Chris Ballard " will be/has been " to Peyton Manning.

It seems that Patrick's source for that information was inaccurate. Following the Patrick report, Mike Chappell of FOX59/CBS4 reported that Colts co-owner/CEO Carlie Irsay-Gordon had not reached out to Manning about the GM role (or any other position).

That obviously could change in the future, but Chappell noted that "[i]t's uncertain if Manning would have an interest if contacted." That has been the prevailing notion in the aftermath of Patrick's report.

From Adam Schefter to Colin Cowherd to Shannon Sharpe , insiders, pundits and former players have questioned if Manning would even be interested in running an NFL team.

"I believe that that job is beneath Peyton Manning," Schefter said on Altitude Sports Radio 92.5 FM on Tuesday. "You think Tom Brady would come back as a GM, or you think he would come back as an owner?

"His family's in Denver. His kids are there. I don't think he wants to go run a day-to-day organization. As much money as he's made in football, as much money as he's made post-football, why is he uprooting his family to go run a day-to-day operations of a football franchise?"

Manning, 50, said in 2024 that running an NFL team wasn't on his radar " in any way ." So, it seems that the two-time Super Bowl champion isn't a likely candidate to return to Indy to fill the team's GM position.

articles.title: ‘(Pat) McAfee Experience Is Coming to a Conclusion,’ ‘Showing Some Cracks’ — NFL Fans React As ESPN Star’s MNF Alt-Cast Gets Beat by ManningCast
articles.summary: Pat McAfee brought his alt-cast to “Monday Night Football” for the first time on Oct. 19.
articles.body:
Pat McAfee brought his alt-cast to "Monday Night Football" for the first time on Oct. 19. "Monday Night Football Field Pass with The Pat McAfee Show" debuted on ESPN2 during the San Francisco 49ers' 23-17 win over the Washington Commanders.

However, the debut drew 351,000 viewers, according to a source cited by The Athletic's Andrew Marchand.

ESPN declined to confirm the figure, "which is not common practice," Marchand wrote. Some fans read the number as a sign of McAfee fatigue catching up with the former Indianapolis Colts punter.

How Pat McAfee's Debut Stacked Up Against the Other Alt-Casts

In its Oct. 11 announcement, ESPN said the show would bring "its high-energy, free-flowing commentary and sideline-driven approach" to the NFL.

The announcement placed McAfee behind an end zone with Dan Orlovsky and Darius Butler and put Connor Campbell, Ty Schmit and Tone Digs in a suite inside the stadium.

Commanders-49ers was the first of five "Monday Night Football" editions. After those come a Week 18 Saturday game and a Super Bowl 61 edition on ESPNU on Feb. 14.

Marchand compared the debut with Peyton and Eli Manning's "ManningCast," reporting that McAfee's audience was "around half of what the Mannings have received."

So did McAfee lose a head-to-head fight with the Mannings? No. The two shows did not air against each other. McAfee's "Monday Night Football" alt-cast only airs during selected weeks when the "ManningCast" is not airing.

The alt-cast that did air against him was "MNF Playbook with Next Gen Stats," ESPN's data and analytics show on NFL Network. Monday was its second "Monday Night Football" appearance of the season.

Sports Business Journal reporter Austin Karp published a breakdown that matched Marchand's ESPN2 figure, showing McAfee was "actually outdrawn."

The Next Gen Stats telecast drew 469,000 viewers, 118,000 more than McAfee by Karp's numbers. The game itself drew 6.688 million viewers on ESPN and 10.312 million on the ABC simulcast.

For comparison, the ManningCast drew 705,000 viewers for its Week 1 Chiefs-Broncos broadcast and 661,000 in Week 2.

One fan wrote , "One can only hope the McAfee experience is coming to a conclusion."

Another fan suggested that "the oversaturation of McAfee may be finally showing some cracks," adding, "Like his style in small doses he's everywhere now."

McAfee is on ESPN even more this season. He currently also holds a full-time role on "Monday Night Countdown," the network's pregame and halftime show.

That comes on top of his central spot on "College GameDay" and the daily afternoon show ESPN licenses from him.

Another fan put it more bluntly : "America has McAfee fatigue. His employer just hasn't figured it out yet."

PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN's Free NFL Playoff Predictor

Another fan joked about what it could mean for the Manning brothers: "They're gonna kick the Mannings off of ESPN2 in favor of McAfee aren't they"

For now, ESPN has the two shows sharing the channel.

McAfee's alt-casts have drawn bigger audiences outside the NFL. ESPN said that since they began in 2022, many editions have averaged over 1 million viewers, and the most-watched drew 2.4 million.

His alt-cast for the College Football Playoff national championship in January drew 1.2 million viewers, according to The Athletic.

His next "Monday Night Football" edition is Nov. 9, when the Buffalo Bills visit the Minnesota Vikings on ESPN2.

articles.title: Bye Week Check-Ins: Week 7
articles.summary: This article looks at the teams on bye in Week 7. Where do they stand, and how can they improve for the rest of the season?
articles.body:
While 28 teams will play in Week 7, four teams will get a bye week as they regroup and look ahead to the rest of the season.

The bye teams show variety: two have started the season well, while the other two haven't had the season they expected so far.

But with a week off, how can these groups regroup and improve for the rest of 2026, or continue their success for the rest of the season?

The first team on its Week 7 bye is Buffalo, off to a great start.

They sit at 5-1 and lead the AFC East, though the Patriots are right there at 4-2.

Joe Brady's first season as head coach has been polarizing offensively, with the Bills leading the NFL in points per game at 32.8. Even crazier, Buffalo is 4-0 this season while allowing 30-plus points , making them the first team in NFL history to have four-plus wins despite allowing 30-plus points through six games.

On that notethat note, though, Buffalo's defense has been much less impressive. The Bills are allowing 28.5 points per game, the 28th most in the NFL through six weeks. They are also 31st in touchdowns allowed and 31st in passing yards allowed per game.

With the trade deadline looming, Buffalo may need to address its defense. its defense

As for the elite offense, Josh Allen continues to be ridiculous, completing 1,504 passes for 1,504 yards and four interceptions. He's also run 48 times for 240 yards and 4 touchdowns, with a 62.5% success rate on his runs.

James Cook continues to hold it down in the backfield for Buffalo, with 117 rushing attempts, 627 yards, and six touchdowns. He's converted 35 first downs on his runs this season.

Tyler Bass's return has also been a welcome addition, as he's converted all 13 of his field-goal attempts so far and 18 of 20 extra-point attempts.

The Bills have few negatives from an offensive and special-teams perspective. The season's outcome will hinge entirely on the defense, and with the bye week coming up, that needs to be Buffalo's focus.

Get this defense right, and the Bills have a legitimate chance at winning a Super Bowl in February.

Between the end-of-overtime debacle in the Giants game and a 1-4-1 record, things haven't been too fun in Washington so far, heading into their bye week.

A healthy Jayden Daniels was supposed to bring better fortune this season, but things hhaven'tgone to plan for the Commanders.

Even more concerning, the one win came without Daniels, and the Commanders are now 0-7-1 in his last eight starts.

Washington isn't particularly good on either side of the ball: 21st in points per game (22.0) and 29th in points allowed per game (28.7).

The Commanders are tied for first in turnover differential at plus-six but still have a minus-40 point differential, which seems difficult, but they're doing it.

They have no rushing weakness, as Jacory Croskey-Merritt leads the team with 239 yards on 67 attempts, and Rachaad White is second with 145 yards on 36 attempts.

Daniels hasn't been great, but he's not terrible either, completing 64.7% of his passes for 759 yards and five touchdowns. On the plus side, he hasn't thrown an interception yet in 2026.

The Commanders still have a thorn in their side: Laremy Tunsil went down before the season started, and Terry McLaurin tore his patellar tendon on Monday night, ending his season.

Washington seems directionless right now, with more questions than answers. Dan Quinn's fate as head coach will likely be the first domino to fall, but many more questions will follow.

As for the rest of the 2026 season, the Commanders will likely slog to the finish line.

The Jaguars may be coming off a tough loss to the Texans in London, but the 2026 season has started well in Jacksonville.

They sit 4-2 and top the AFC South as they enter their bye week, ranking top-ten in both points scored and allowed per game.

The Jaguars score 25.7 points per game (8th in the NFL) and allow 17.3 (3rd in the NFL), making them a formidable opponent on both sides of the ball.

Trevor Lawrence has been great, completing 65.2% of his passes for 1,480 yards, 14 touchdowns, and four interceptions; his running back Bhayshul Tuten is solid as well.

In the receiving game, Parker Washington, Jakobi Meyers, and Brenton Strange have led the way.

The two real negatives have been Brian Thomas Jr.'s play, which has almost completely stopped the pass defense as a whole.

Despite ranking 3rd in points allowed, the Jaguars are 30th in passing yards allowed per game and 30th per play . Some of that could be from playing ahead a lot, but they still need to fix it.

Despite the few negatives, Jacksonville looks like a team that will keep playing well into January.

As long as they stay healthy, this bye week should be about rest, because most of what the Jaguars have done under Liam Coen has worked. Now they have to keep doing those things, and it should be another 10-plus-win season in Duval County.

And now for last and certainly least, the Los Angeles Chargers.

Calling the 2026 season a disaster would be an understatement, as the Chargers have reached their bye week and still hhaven'twon a game. They are 0-6.The

The McDaniel experiment has been horrible, and the offensive line has been even worse.

Despite being pressured on just 24.5% of dropbacks (3rd lowest in the league), the Chargers allow the highest pressure rate in the NFL at 46%, and Justin Herbert has been sacked on 10.4% of dropbacks, the 2nd-highest rate in the league.

Overall, they rank 30th in points per game (15.0) and 22nd in points allowed per game (25.2).

The 2026 Chargers are also the first team since the 2009 Titans to start 0-6, average 115 or fewer points per game, and give up 15-plus giveaways through those six games. That Titans team recovered to finish 8-8, but the same fate likely doesn't await this Los Angeles team.

ddoesn't020 Herbert has been the most pressured, sacked, and hit quarterback in the NFL, and nothing seems to be changing for the Chargers.

He's been bad, yes, but how much of the blame is on the quarterback when the team fails him over and over?

Overall, Herbert has completed 59.4% of his passes in 2026 for 1.141 yards, five touchdowns, and eight interceptions.

The Chargers' leading rusher is Omarion Hampton, but hhe'saveraging just 3.6 yards per carry behind his offensive line.

There aren't many good things to say about the Chargers right now, and for a team that lost just six games in 2025, being 0-6 at your week seven bye week is an unmitigated disaster. There's no other way around it.

As of right now, the Chargers and Dolphins are the only two winless teams remaining in the NFL (Miami is 0-5 and had a week six bye week), and they will meet in Miami on Sunday, Dec 27, where the loser could very well be in line to select first in the 2027 NFL Draft.

As it stands, that might be the biggest game left on the Chargers' schedule.

As for this bye week and what comes after, the Chargers will play the Rams on Nov 1 as they try to win their first game of the season.

Buffalo and Jacksonville have lots to look forward to, while Washington has been disappointing and injured yet again, but they could have some surprise wins up their sleeve as the season winds down.

As for the Chargers, they're in a league of their own when it comes to disappointing seasons, and they've had almost no positives so far in 2026.

It'll be interesting to see where these teams land as the rest of the 2026 season unfolds. Will Los Angeles and Washington have new coaches/coordinators? Will Buffalo finally get over the hump under Brady? Can Jacksonville truly ascend into a premier AFC contender?

articles.title: Jets need to stay patient with rookie D'Angelo Ponds
articles.summary: The New York Jets need to stay patient with the development of rookie cornerback D'Angelo Ponds.
articles.body:
The New York Jets were expected to receive significant contributions from their 2026 NFL Draft class. Through Week 6, it's been a mixed bag. No. 2 overall edge David Bailey is getting up-and-down results while generally being impressive. Fellow first-round picks in Tight end Kenyon Sadiq has been hot-and-cold, and receiver Omar Cooper Jr. recently got back from injury .

One rookie who has made almost no impact whatsoever is cornerback D'Angelo Ponds. The 50th overall selection has played just 34 defensive snaps.

The Jets need to stay patient with Ponds' development despite the current frustrations.

Ponds has not maximized his limited opportunities. In fact, the former Indiana standout has done the opposite. Currently, Ponds' 26.7 grade via Pro Football Focus ranks 163rd (dead last) among all 163 CBs to play any defensive snaps in 2026. He was the team's lowest-graded defensive player versus the New England Patriots in Week 6 (26.4).

Ponds has been whistled for two penalties in limited action. He's given up two explosive passing plays to the opposition, for gains of 21 and 39. There's good reasons why he continues to play behind starting nickelback Jarvis Brownlee Jr.

Ponds' offseason development was hampered by a training camp injury. The versatile DB didn't even make his regular-season debut until Week 3. It's extremely difficult for a rookie to be thrown into the fire after missing crucial preseason reps. That's what Ponds is currently dealing with, and his trial by fire is occuring weekly.

Jets Wire will continue to provide updates throughout the 2026 NFL season.

articles.title: NFL Fines Mike Vrabel, Aaron Glenn and Nick Sirianni $750,000 Combined
articles.summary: Mike Vrabel and Aaron Glenn faced off in Week 6, when the Patriots beat the Jets 26-19. Nick Sirianni’s Eagles also struggled that day, falling to the Panthe...
articles.body:
Mike Vrabel and Aaron Glenn faced off in Week 6, when the Patriots beat the Jets 26-19. Nick Sirianni 's Eagles also struggled that day, falling to the Panthers 25-14. All three coaches have faced scrutiny this season, and a league announcement this week has now placed them in the same conversation. The message behind it reaches well beyond a single game.

Mike Vrabel, Aaron Glenn and Nick Sirianni get $250K NFL fines each

The NFL has fined Patriots coach Mike Vrabel, Jets coach Aaron Glenn and Eagles coach Nick Sirianni $250,000 each for their conduct toward game officials, according to Sports Illustrated's Albert Breer. ESPN later confirmed Sirianni's fine through a source.

The league brought up the topic during this week's owners meetings, where it addressed rising tension between coaches, players and officials. The three fines were cited as examples of that push.

The financial hit may never land, though. "That, of course, is a pretty stiff penalty and a clear statement," Albert Breer added. "I've also heard that the fines are in abeyance, meaning they'd be on hold, and could be repealed with good behavior."

The reports did not name the incidents behind each fine. Vrabel was flagged for unsportsmanlike conduct in Week 4 after criticizing a call during New England's 29-26 win over Buffalo. He later said, "I have to be better in those moments."

Glenn was shown on camera in an animated exchange with officials during the Jets' Week 6 loss, but he has not spoken about it.

Sirianni has a history of animated moments with referees, though his specific incident was not identified.

However, the announcement quickly drew a strong response online, and fans were far from silent.

Fans respond to the NFL fines on Vrabel, Glenn and Sirianni

Officials and coaches are now at the center of a heated debate, and fans quickly weighed in under Ari Meirov's post on X. Many replies targeted the officials, while others mocked the fines.

One fan wrote , "Refs honestly need to be taken to a back alley"

Another fan added , "Refs already have enough say in the game, now you want coaches to not argue with crappy calls? Refs need fined for all the bad flags they throw"

A third mocked , "On hold and could be rescinded if they have better behavior" is hilarious lmao

Another fan slammed , "Man these refs… respectfully of course"

One user noted , "The league is making history with the amount of calls and these coaches have every right to give these cheating ass refs grief.@nflcommish GOODELL IS RUINING THE NFL. RUINED SO MUCH ALREADYl"

The debate has grown all month. The NFL suspended line judge Jeff Seeman for two games and referee Adrian Hill for one game earlier this month, and Peyton Manning also criticized the referees on air. Fans now see the coach fines as another test of who gets held accountable.

Now, the Patriots (4-2) visit the Bears on Thursday night, the Jets (2-4) host the Dolphins on Sunday, and the Eagles (2-4) face the Cowboys on Monday. All three coaches must now stay calm on the sideline to keep the fines on hold.
